description: The Caravan Gallery is a unique documentary photography project and exhibition focused on Croydon's built environment. The Caravan Gallery photograph the sur/reality of everyday life and work with communities to explore people's connection to place, exhibiting their photographs of the area in a small caravan.

factsheet.heading: The Caravan Gallery
paragraphs: The Caravan Gallery is a unique mobile art project founded by Jan Williams and Chris Teasdale in 2000. Operating from a converted touring caravan, the gallery has spent 26 years documenting and celebrating everyday British life, taking art directly to communities across the UK and internationally. Working at the intersection of documentary photography, community engagement and contemporary art, The Caravan Gallery is equally at home in festivals, town centres, museums, and international biennials.

factsheet.heading: Croydon: Pride of Place
paragraphs: During Open House Festival, The Caravan Gallery will be popping up around Croydon Town Centre to share their travelling exhibition exploring Croydon's buildings and people. The project captures the character of the borough through the people and places that shape it. Their photographs will be exhibited in a travelling caravan gallery across Croydon during Open House Festival week, including College Square 16-17 September.
